question: Why did thermogravimetric analysis show the macaw oil to be stable up to about 450 C?
expect: premise false: measurable degradation began around 300 C, so continuous operation should stay below about 300 C (abstract; TGA section)
rendered: According to the text, thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) showed the macaw oil to be stable up to about 300°C, not 450°C. The text states that the oil shows an onset of measurable volatilization/decomposition with ∼10% mass loss at ∼300 °C, followed by a major degradation stage up to ∼480 °C that accounts for ≈95% of the initial mass.
